newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, seen pausing for breather.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, seen pausing for breather.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in uneventful trade on Wednesday and traders expected prices to stagnate until a new wave of investments sweeps the market.
"Stocks which have been on the rise recently, like (food processor) Podravka and some hoteliers, will lose breath," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage.
He predicted larger investor interest for bank stocks such as Dalmatinska and Privredna Banka, that are for the moment only traded over-the-counter, spurring their liquidity in the days to come.
Six of 13 traded issues rose, four fell, two were flat and one was sold for the first time in months. Volume rose very slightly to 8,909 shares, and turnover to 4.3 million kuna.
Zagrebacka Banka was not traded, and market participants said its shares, which changed hands at 1,860 kuna Tuesday, may be too expensive for ordinary punters.
Zagrebacka's C-series bearer shares jumped 130 kuna to 730, but only one unit was sold. Its E-series preference stock remained flat at 1,050 kuna on volume of 390 shares.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva dipped 13 kuna or 0.2 percent to 480 kuna on volume of 1,117.
The price was seen in line with what its 1/5 GDRs are fetching on the London Stock Exchange, $16.515 on Wednesday, but traders did not see it as an obstacle to a further rise.

"Pliva may now fetch higher prices in Zagreb than London from now on because there are many small investors who want to buy its shares. They are now prepared to pay 500 kuna and more," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.
Food processor Podravka was again most active on volume of 4,271 units, but it closed flat at 350 kuna, after trading in a 340-350 range.
Istrian hotelier Jadranturist led decliners, losing 25 kuna or 7.04 percent to 330 kuna with 190 units changing hands.
Laguna, which said it expected some 4-5 million kuna profit for 1996 after a much larger 1995 loss, was also 20 kuna weaker at close. It ended at 1,480 kuna on volume of 777 units.

Porec's Riviera was the biggest gainer among hotel stocks. It added 11 kuna or 6.92 percent to 170 kuna with 867 shares sold. All other hoteliers, including the Dalmatian Suncani Hvar, also continued to gain.
Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf rose 1,500 kuna or 18.75 percent to 9,000 kuna but sold only 19 shares.

Croatia Osiguranje insurer's B-series stock traded at 1,500 kuna for the first time since early July last year, when its face value was under 23 kuna. The shares have since been amalgamated to produce a nominal price of 1,400 kuna.
Chocolate maker Kras lost a further five kuna to 485, with 130 shares changing hands.
